# Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents

Beining Wu Wu.Beining@jacks.sdstate.edu Affiliation: Zihao Ding
Zihao.Ding@jacks.sdstate.edu Affiliation: Jun Huang
Jun.Huang@sdstate.edu Affiliation: Department of Electrical Engineering
and Computer Science, South Dakota State University

###### Abstract

Self-improving GUI agents keep the trajectories they produce and return
them to the agent, by fine-tuning or by retrieval into the prompt, and
studies that compare the two destinations disagree. We attribute this to
the unit of experience: a trajectory bundles items with different
properties, so a conclusion about the bundle depends on its mix. To
address this, (i) we introduce _component routing_, which splits the
experience into locators, procedures, state facts and lessons and sends
each component to the context or to the weights, compared on the same
items across three backbone families, two environments and three seeds.
One pool has two destinations: locators and lessons win in the weights,
procedures and state facts in the context. (ii) We fit a rule in two
properties measured before any training, recurrence and
state-conditionality; it recovers the destination of a held-out backbone
family in 24 of 24 cells, two interventions move a component toward the
boundary, and routing by the rule beats every whole-trajectory baseline
and, by +3.5 points on average, the better single destination of each
backbone. (iii) We identify how training and producer–consumer
differences change the value of the two destinations: note readout
decreases after the same component is written into the weights, most for
the items that recur most, context gains increase with the information
gap, and weights gains decrease with the policy gap. Code and data will
be released.

## 1 Introduction

GUI agents that operate phones and desktops are increasingly improved
with their own traces: an agent runs a batch of tasks, the trajectories
are kept, and the experience is returned to the agent.

![Refer to caption](2610.01787v1/fig2_routing_arial.png)

Figure 2: A motivating example. G recurs across tasks and goes to the
weights; P matters only on the preview screen and stays in context.
Screens are illustrative.

Where that experience should go is an open decision. One line of work
fine-tunes the agent on its successful trajectories; another keeps the
trajectories, or notes distilled from them, in a library that is
retrieved into the prompt. On MobileGym, an 8B agent whose whole pool
goes to the weights gains 7.1 points of held-out success and one whose
whole pool goes to the context gains 8.0, yet the two destinations
disagree on which parts of the pool are responsible: the components that
gain most in the weights are the ones that gain least in context
(Figure [1](#S0.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")a).
Figure [2](#S1.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
shows the smallest version of this. One trajectory on a weather
application teaches where the search field is and that a city is saved
by tapping Add on its preview; fine-tuning on the whole trajectory
learns the first and loses the second.

We attribute this to the unit of experience. Existing methods treat a
trajectory as the unit: success-filtered fine-tuning distills whole
trajectories into the weights ([Zhang et al., 2026](#bib.bib68); [Men
et al., 2026](#bib.bib36); [Fan et al., 2026](#bib.bib14)), and
retrieval keeps whole trajectories or trajectory-level skills in context
([Xiong et al., 2026](#bib.bib65); [Hu et al., 2026](#bib.bib23); [Sui
et al., 2026](#bib.bib40)). Comparisons of the two destinations reach
opposite conclusions: internalized hints beat the prompt on tool tasks
([Alakuijala et al., 2026](#bib.bib3)), prompt-side updates beat
gradient updates on web tasks ([Li et al., 2026](#bib.bib31); [Agrawal
et al., 2026](#bib.bib2)), and the same skill representation helps one
task and hurts another ([Liu et al., 2026b](#bib.bib34)). A trajectory
bundles items with different properties, so any conclusion about the
bundle depends on its mix.

Deciding where a piece of experience belongs requires two things: a
property of the piece that can be measured before any training, and a
comparison in which both destinations consume the same items and are
read on the same held-out tasks. Existing comparisons pit one whole
pipeline against another, so the items differ before the destinations do
([Alakuijala et al., 2026](#bib.bib3); [Gou et al., 2026](#bib.bib18)),
and none asks it per component.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

We answer this question with _component routing_. Experience is split
into four components, locators, procedures, state facts and lessons, and
each component is characterized by two properties measured on the pool
before any training: _recurrence_, how often its key comes up in
unrelated tasks, and _state-conditionality_, how much its usefulness
depends on the current state matching its source state. Each component
is then sent to the context, to the weights, or to both, on the same
items and the same held-out instances, across three backbone families
and two environments.

Three observations follow. The four components split by destination: the
route gain, weights minus context, is +4.9 points for locators and +1.5
for lessons, $`-`$4.2 for procedures and $`-`$4.1 for state facts
(Figure [1](#S0.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")a).
The two properties account for the split: a rule fitted with the tested
backbone held out recovers the sign in 24 of 24 cells, an eightfold
training dose moves procedures toward the weights by +3.5 points, and
stripping the state condition from state facts costs 3.4. Routing each
component by the rule exceeds the better single destination of each
backbone by +3.5 points on average over three backbones and two
environments, and the reverse assignment by +7.8
(Figure [1](#S0.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")b).

Contributions. (i) A measurement of where an agent’s own experience
belongs: four components, two pool-level properties, and a paired
comparison of the context and the weights on the same items across three
backbones, two environments and three seeds. (ii) A routing rule in
recurrence and state-conditionality that recovers the winning
destination of every component on a held-out backbone family, with two
interventions that move a component toward the boundary. (iii) An
account of how training, information gaps and policy gaps shape
experience reuse: the readout of high-recurrence notes falls to 16
percent once the same items are in the weights, most for the items that
recur most, and the context route gains from an information gap while
the weights route loses to a policy gap.

## 2 Related Work

#### Two destinations for experience.

Self-improving agents return their own experience along two routes.
_Fine-tuning_ writes it into the weights ([Ding & Huang,
2026](#bib.bib7); [Ding et al., 2026b](#bib.bib10); [Ding et al.,
2026c](#bib.bib11); [Wu & Huang, 2026b](#bib.bib49); [Wu et al.,
2026c](#bib.bib55); [Wu et al., 2026d](#bib.bib56); [Wu et al.,
2026i](#bib.bib61)), on the agent’s rollouts ([Zhang et al.,
2026](#bib.bib68); [Men et al., 2026](#bib.bib36); [Ding et al.,
2026a](#bib.bib9); [Huang et al., 2025a](#bib.bib24); [Huang et al.,
2025b](#bib.bib25); [Wu & Wu, 2023](#bib.bib50); [Wu et al.,
2023](#bib.bib51); [Wu et al., 2025](#bib.bib52)), on skills extracted
from them ([Fan et al., 2026](#bib.bib14); [Wu et al.,
2026k](#bib.bib63)), or by distilling a helpful context into the
parameters ([Alakuijala et al., 2026](#bib.bib3); [Gou et al.,
2026](#bib.bib18); [He et al., 2026](#bib.bib21)). _Retrieval_ keeps it
in a store that is read into the prompt ([Wu & Huang,
2026a](#bib.bib48); [Wu et al., 2026a](#bib.bib53); [Wu et al.,
2026e](#bib.bib57)): trajectory and skill libraries ([Xiong et al.,
2026](#bib.bib65); [Hu et al., 2026](#bib.bib23); [Wei et al.,
2026](#bib.bib47)), evolved prompts ([Agrawal et al., 2026](#bib.bib2)),
or logit-level updates without gradients ([Li et al.,
2026](#bib.bib31)). Comparisons of the two disagree, fine-tuning leading
on tool tasks ([Alakuijala et al., 2026](#bib.bib3)) and the prompt on
generalization and on knowledge written in sequence ([Lampinen et al.,
2025](#bib.bib30); [Wang et al., 2026b](#bib.bib46)); theory ties the
answer to the data ([Chan et al., 2025](#bib.bib5)), and recent systems
route by volatility ([Ji et al., 2026](#bib.bib26)) or run both routes
under one budget ([Kim et al., 2026a](#bib.bib27)). All of them take a
whole trajectory as the unit and change the pipeline with the
destination; component routing holds the items fixed and compares the
two destinations per component.

#### Experience forms in GUI agents.

GUI agents are trained on trajectories, human demonstrations at first
([Wang et al., 2025](#bib.bib45); [Liu et al., 2026a](#bib.bib33)) and
now their own rollouts in verifiable environments ([Wu et al.,
2026j](#bib.bib62); [Wang et al., 2026a](#bib.bib44)). What is kept from
a trajectory varies: skills distilled into the weights ([Fan et al.,
2026](#bib.bib14)), skill cards retrieved or distilled ([Liu et al.,
2026b](#bib.bib34)), hindsight-relabelled experience ([Men et al.,
2026](#bib.bib36)), and memories built to survive interface change ([Sun
et al., 2026](#bib.bib41)). Diagnoses show that trajectory fine-tuning
learns interface shortcuts as readily as semantics ([Gu et al.,
2026](#bib.bib19)) and that a form which helps grounding can hurt action
prediction ([Liu et al., 2026b](#bib.bib34)). Each of these works fixes
one form and one destination. We split one pool into four components and
let two measured properties decide where each goes.

#### Producer, consumer and fragility.

Whether self-generated experience helps depends on who produced it and
who consumes it ([Ding et al., 2025](#bib.bib8); [Ding et al.,
2026d](#bib.bib12); [Duan et al., 2023](#bib.bib13); [Fang et al.,
2025a](#bib.bib15); [Fang et al., 2025b](#bib.bib16); [Fang et al.,
2025c](#bib.bib17); [Pan et al., 2023](#bib.bib37); [Tchalla et al.,
2026](#bib.bib42); [Wu et al., 2026b](#bib.bib54); [Wu et al.,
2026f](#bib.bib58); [Wu et al., 2026g](#bib.bib59); [Wu et al.,
2026h](#bib.bib60); [Xing et al., 2025](#bib.bib64)): a stronger agent
can specialize a smaller one through its weights ([Kim et al.,
2026b](#bib.bib28)), shared trajectory stores help consumers on either
side of the ability gap ([Kim et al., 2026c](#bib.bib29)), synthesized
tools help only models weaker than their builder ([Lou et al.,
2026](#bib.bib35)), and the gain from a harness changes with base
ability in opposite directions across studies ([Lin et al.,
2026](#bib.bib32); [Wei et al., 2026](#bib.bib47)). Self-improvement
loops are also fragile: memory gains move with seeds, task order and
backbone ([Ye et al., 2026](#bib.bib67)), much of what a module stores
comes from failed or falsely successful runs ([Hajimiri et al.,
2026](#bib.bib20); [Advani, 2026](#bib.bib1)), and repeated
internalization collapses rather than compounds ([Chen et al.,
2026](#bib.bib6)). These studies report the net effect of a producer or
a consumer. We separate it into an information gap and a policy gap,
measured on one pool across three backbone families and a size ladder.

## 3 Experimental Setup

![Refer to caption](2610.01787v1/figN.png)

Figure 3: Overview. Whole-history reuse (left) against component
routing: (A) profile every item of the pool, (B) compare both
destinations per component (middle), and reuse each component from its
destination on a new task (right).

Component routing splits an agent’s own experience into four components
and sends each to the context or to the weights of the same agent
(Figure [3](#S3.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
It treats a trajectory not as one unit but as a bundle of items whose
properties can be measured before any route is trained; Appendix A gives
the details.

#### Problem formulation.

An agent with policy $`\pi`$ runs a batch of tasks on a fixed set of
applications and keeps every trajectory, successful or not; each step
records the screenshot, the structured application state, the on-screen
elements, and the action with its target element. This batch is the
_experience pool_ $`E`$. An extractor maps $`E`$ to four item sets
$`D_{c}`$, $`c\in\{G,P,F,L\}`$, where $`G`$, $`P`$, $`F`$ and $`L`$
denote locators, procedures, state facts and lessons, and every item
$`d\in D_{c}`$ carries a key $`k(d)`$ that identifies it across
episodes. A destination turns an item set into a policy: the _context
route_ $`{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}}`$ retrieves items of
$`D_{c}`$ into the prompt at each step, the _weights route_
$`{\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W_{c}}`$ fine-tunes $`\pi`$ on them,
and the _coexistence_ arm
$`{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}}{+}{\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W_{c}}`$
does both. Let $`T`$ be the set of held-out task instances and
$`u(x;\rho)\in\{0,1\}`$ the checker’s verdict on instance $`x`$ under
policy $`\rho`$, so that $`U(\rho)=|T|^{-1}\sum_{x\in T}u(x;\rho)`$ is
held-out success. The quantity this paper measures is the _route gain_

|     |                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle\Delta(c)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentW!45}$\displaystyle U({\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W*{c}})$}\;-\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle U({\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C*{c}})$}`$ |     | (1)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|     |                            | $`\displaystyle=\;\frac{1}{                                                                                                                                                                                     | T   | }\sum*{x\in T}\Bigl[\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentW!45}$\displaystyle u\bigl(x;{\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W*{c}}\bigr)$}\;-\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle u\bigl(x;{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C\_{c}}\bigr)$}\;\Bigr],\qquad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,one paired comparison per instance}}`$ |     |     |

where $`\Delta(c)>0`$ means that component $`c`$ is better off in the
weights.

#### Components.

Every item carries a key, a note that the context route serves and a
sample that the weights route trains on. A _locator_ says where a named
element sits on a screen: its key is application, role and element name,
and its sample pairs the screenshot with a click on the element. A
_procedure_ is a short run of action targets that recurs inside a task
family: its key is three consecutive targets, its note gives the subgoal
sequence, and its sample predicts the next action with the subgoals as
the thought. A _state fact_ is a precondition that must hold before an
action succeeds, extracted from a failed and a successful attempt at the
same target: its key is application, target and predicate, and its
sample predicts the action with the predicate as the thought. A _lesson_
pairs an action that failed in a state with the one that later succeeded
there: its key is application, state and failed target, and its sample
is the preference pair. A rule-based extractor produces $`D_{c}`$.

#### State signature.

The state at a step $`x`$ is summarized by a signature $`S(x)`$, the
application route together with the set of path–value pairs of the
environment state without volatile fields such as timestamps; on
AndroidWorld, whose application state is not exposed, the signature is
the set of visible accessibility nodes, the view a deployed agent has
(Appendix [B.1](#A2.SS1 "B.1 Environments and Splits ‣ Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
Steps of one application are compared by the Jaccard similarity
$`J(x,y)=|S(x)\cap S(y)|\,/\,|S(x)\cup S(y)|`$; a match is _exact_,
written $`\mathrm{E}`$, when $`J(x,y)\geq\theta`$ with $`\theta=0.9`$,
and _relaxed_, written $`\mathrm{R}`$, when
$`\theta^{\prime}\leq J(x,y)<\theta`$ with $`\theta^{\prime}=0.5`$.
Retrieval and both properties use these tiers.

#### Recurrence and state-conditionality.

For an item $`d`$, let $`P_{d}`$ be the episodes in which $`d`$ is
produced, $`N_{p}`$ the episodes of the pool that run on the same
application as episode $`p`$ but on a different task template, and
$`K_{q}`$ the set of keys of all items extracted from episode $`q`$.
_Recurrence_ is

|     |                        |                                      |        |                               |
| --- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------ | ----------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle r(d)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\frac{1}{ | P\_{d} | }\sum*{p\in P*{d}}\;\frac{1}{ | N\_{p} | }\sum*{q\in N*{p}}\mathds{1}\bigl[\,k(d)\in K_{q}\,\bigr],\qquad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,share of unrelated tasks where the key returns}}`$ |     | (2) |
|     | $`\displaystyle r(c)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\frac{1}{ | D\_{c} | }\sum*{d\in D*{c}}r(d),`$     |        |                                                                                                                                                                                   |

where the component summary is a mean because the item distribution is
right-skewed. _State-conditionality_ is how much the usefulness of an
item depends on the current state matching its source state. Let
$`\Omega_{\tau}(d)`$ be the pairs of occurrences of $`k(d)`$ whose
states match at tier $`\tau\in\{\mathrm{E},\mathrm{R}\}`$, and
$`\phi_{d}(x)`$ the payload of $`d`$ observed at $`x`$, the position of
a locator or the next target of a procedure. Before any route is trained
we use the proxy

|     |                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                   |                                                                                                                                  |
| --- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle a_{\tau}(d)`$  | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\frac{1}{                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | \Omega\_{\tau}(d) | }\sum*{(x,y)\in\Omega*{\tau}(d)}\mathds{1}\bigl[\,\phi_{d}(x)\simeq\phi_{d}(y)\,\bigr],\qquad\tau\in\{\mathrm{E},\mathrm{R}\},`$ |     | (3) |
|     | $`\displaystyle\kappa_{0}(d)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;1-\frac{a_{\mathrm{R}}(d)}{a_{\mathrm{E}}(d)},\qquad\kappa_{0}(c)\;\triangleq\;\operatorname*{med}_{d\in\tilde{D}_{c}}\,\kappa_{0}(d),\qquad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,$\tilde{D}\_{c}$: items with pairs at both tiers}}`$ |                   |                                                                                                                                  |

where $`\simeq`$ is payload agreement, within 0.5 percent of the screen
diagonal for a position and identity for a target. Once the context
route has run with exact-only retrieval
$`{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}^{\mathrm{E}}}`$ and relaxed-only
retrieval $`{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}^{\mathrm{R}}}`$, the
online quantity

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
\kappa(c)\;\triangleq\;\frac{\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle U({\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}^{\mathrm{E}}})$}\;-\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle U({\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}^{\mathrm{R}}})$}}{\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle U({\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}^{\mathrm{E}}})$}\;-\;U_{0}},\qquad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,share of the context gain that needs an exact state match}}
``` |  | (4) |

confirms the proxy, where $`U_{0}=U(\pi)`$ is the success of the agent
without experience. Both $`r`$ and $`\kappa_{0}`$ come from the pool
alone, so a practitioner has them before any training decision.

#### Two destinations.

The context route keeps $`D_{c}`$ in a library indexed by application
and key. At a step $`x`$, the items of the same application are ranked
by $`J(x,\cdot)`$ against their source states, and the five best are
appended to the prompt as notes, exact matches first; the rest of the
prompt is the base agent’s, character for character. The weights route
fine-tunes the backbone on the samples of the same items with low-rank
adaptation ([Hu et al., 2022](#bib.bib22), LoRA;), one configuration for
all backbones and arms
(Appendix [C](#A3 "Appendix C Training Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")),
by direct preference optimization ([Rafailov et al., 2023](#bib.bib38))
for lessons and supervised fine-tuning for the other components; every
trained arm reaches a token accuracy of at least 0.90 on a held-in
development split. The tuned model is merged and served with the base
agent’s prompt, and
$`{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{c}}{+}{\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W_{c}}`$
serves it with the same notes.

#### Reference arms.

Every backbone also runs without experience and with undivided whole
trajectories: success-filtered fine-tuning on entire trajectories,
retrieval of one similar trajectory, retrieval of ten step-level records
by task similarity, and context-then-distill. Three controls probe the
instrument: random notes from other applications, notes with shuffled
keys and contents, and training samples with shuffled labels. A retry
arm keeps the first of three attempts that the agent declares complete,
and three aggregate arms send all components to context, all to the
weights, or each to the destination the fitted rule assigns
(Appendix [B](#A2 "Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).

#### Evaluation setup.

We evaluate on MobileGym ([Wu et al., 2026j](#bib.bib62)) and
AndroidWorld ([Rawles et al., 2025](#bib.bib39)). MobileGym is a
simulated phone with 20 applications and 416 task templates (160
training, 256 test) whose checker compares the application state to the
task target; the same state is readable at every step, which makes the
keys above well defined. A fixed rank rule holds out 5 applications; the
remaining training templates form the pool (122 templates), and the test
templates form two held-out tiers, new templates on practiced
applications (165) and templates on unseen applications (59), with up to
8 instances per template and seed (1 106 paired instances per seed).
AndroidWorld has 116 tasks on 20 real applications and an accessibility
tree; 12 applications provide experience, 8 are held out, and 58
held-out tasks are run with four instances each (232 paired instances
per seed). Held-out success is decided by each environment’s
deterministic checker, with no model judge. Every arm of a backbone is
evaluated on the same instances, and differences are read with a paired
bootstrap over instances (10 000 resamples, 95 percent intervals),
pooled over the two tiers and per tier. Producer and consumer are the
same model from three families in the 7–8B range, GUI-Owl-1.5-8B ([Xu
et al., 2026](#bib.bib66), GUI-Owl-8B below;), ScaleCUA-7B ([Liu et al.,
2026a](#bib.bib33)) and Qwen3-VL-8B ([Bai et al., 2025](#bib.bib4)); a
same-family ladder, Qwen3-VL 4B, 8B and 32B, serves the
producer–consumer measurements. Pool sampling, training and instance
sampling are controlled by three seeds, and the analysis of every result
was fixed before the runs. Splits, instances and cost are in Appendices
B and H.

## 4 Observations

This section reports what the pool and the two destinations show before
any rule is fitted. Every gain is a paired difference on the same
held-out instances, with 95 percent intervals from the paired bootstrap.

![Refer to caption](2610.01787v1/fig3.png)

Figure 4: Components split by destination. (a, b) Route gain
$`\Delta(c)`$ per backbone on MobileGym and AndroidWorld, with 95
percent intervals; (c) gain of each destination over the base agent,
pooled over backbones, one dot per backbone; (d) the pool on the plane
of recurrence and state-conditionality, with the component summary of
each backbone.

### 4.1 Components Split by Destination

#### Route gains by component.

Figure [4](#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")(a, b)
shows the route gain of each component, backbone and environment.
Locators are better off in the weights on every backbone and in both
environments (+4.9 points pooled over backbones on MobileGym),
procedures and state facts are better off in the context ($`-`$4.2 and
$`-`$4.1), and lessons lean toward the weights by a margin whose
interval includes zero in half of the cells (+1.5). The sign pattern
does not depend on the backbone: the twelve MobileGym cells agree across
the three families, and the AndroidWorld cells, whose state signature is
read from the screen, repeat the pattern with the wider intervals of a
smaller task set. *Both destinations help every component.* Against the
base agent and pooled over backbones
(Figure [4](#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")c),
the context gains between +1.8 and +5.2 points and the weights between
+0.8 and +6.7; what differs is which route helps more, the weights for
locators (+6.7 against +1.8) and the context for procedures (+5.2
against +1.0). *Coexistence adds little where the weights already win.*
Serving the notes on top of the tuned model adds +0.1 points for
locators and +3.5 for state facts, so the context remains useful exactly
for the components that the context wins. *The components differ before
any training.*
Figure [4](#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")(d)
places the items on the plane of the two properties. Procedures almost
never recur outside their task family (mean recurrence 0.05) and are
state-conditioned (0.66); locators recur (0.39) and are nearly
state-free (0.10); state facts and lessons recur (0.32 and 0.45) and are
state-conditioned (0.56 and 0.53). The three backbones place every
component in the same region of the plane.

  Observation 1. *Split by component, one pool has opposite winning
destinations: locators, and weakly lessons, in the weights; procedures
and state facts in the context; on three backbone families and two
environments.*

### 4.2 Producer and Consumer

Figure 5: Producer and consumer. (a) Gain from the procedures of a
producer of each size, read from the context (solid) or written into the
weights (dashed); filled markers train on the consumer’s own procedures
only. (b) One consumer, five producers, three destinations.

#### Producers and consumers.

Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Producer and Consumer ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")(a)
follows the Qwen3-VL family across sizes, in a batch where every
procedures adapter trains on the same number of samples
(Appendix [B.1](#A2.SS1 "B.1 Environments and Splits ‣ Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
Procedures read from the context help every consumer whoever produced
them, and larger producers help more: the 8B consumer gains +3.6 points
from its own procedures, +4.8 from those of the 32B model and +2.2 from
those of the 4B model, and the 32B consumer still gains +3.2 from the
procedures of the 8B model. The same items written into the weights
follow a different rule. Fine-tuning the 8B consumer on the procedures
of the 4B model changes it by $`-`$2.3 points, on those of the 32B model
by $`-`$1.4, and on those of another family by $`-`$7.5
(Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Producer and Consumer ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")b),
while its own procedures give +0.9. *The damage is policy mismatch, not
information.* The same other-family pool read from the context gives
+3.6, and a producer of the other family retrained on the consumer’s own
successes brings the weights route back to $`-`$2.0. *Most of the
weights gain on own procedures is practice.* Fine-tuning on the
consumer’s own procedures alone, without any transferred item, gives
+0.6 against +0.9 with all samples, and the two agree within 1.1 points
on all five consumers
(Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Producer and Consumer ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")a,
filled markers), so the weights route pays for what the consumer already
does more than for what it learns.

  Observation 2. *Notes help regardless of who produced them, and more
so from a stronger producer; fine-tuning helps only when producer and
consumer are the same model, and most of its gain is practice on the
consumer’s own trajectories.*

### 4.3 Readout after Training

Figure 6: Readout after training. (a) Share of probed steps whose action
changes after a note is read, before and after the same items are in the
weights; (b) the after-to-before ratio against the component’s
recurrence.

#### Readout probe.

The readout probe replays a decision step with and without a retrieved
note and records whether the action changes. Before training, a note
changes the action in 42 percent of the probed steps, from 33 percent
for procedures to 48 percent for lessons, at about the same rate on
every consumer
(Figure [6](#S4.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 4.3 Readout after Training ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")a).
After the same items are in the weights, the rate falls to 16 percent
for locators and 15 percent for lessons but only to 22 percent for
procedures, and the after-to-before ratio falls with the recurrence of
the component
(Figure [6](#S4.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 4.3 Readout after Training ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")b,
Spearman $`-`$0.92). The same holds among the items of one component:
split into thirds by recurrence, the ratio falls from 0.73 to 0.11 for
locators and from 0.63 to 0.11 for lessons
(Table [E.4](#A5.T4 "Table E.4 ‣ E.4 Readout ‣ Appendix E Full Results ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
*Redundancy rather than conflict.* The drop is largest for lessons and
locators, the two components that recur most and for which coexistence
added the least above, and smallest for procedures, the component for
which the context keeps its value after training. A note is read when it
carries something the weights do not yet hold, and a component that
recurs is the one the weights absorb.

  Observation 3. *Training on a component makes its notes redundant, and
the more the component recurs, the less its notes are read afterwards.*

## 5 The Routing Rule

This section fits a rule in the two pool measurements, tests it on
held-out backbone families, and examines interventions, training and
version changes.

### 5.1 A Rule in Two Properties

#### Held-out fit.

Each component has one destination across backbone families, and a
linear rule in the two properties recovers it on a family it has not
seen. We score a component by its recurrence against its
state-conditionality and fit the score to the sign of the route gain,
holding out one family at a time. With $`\mathcal{C}`$ the twenty-four
cells of both environments, $`\mathcal{C}_{f}`$ the eight cells of
family $`f`$ and $`I(c)`$ the interval of $`\Delta(c)`$,

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle s_{\theta}(c)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentW!45}$\displaystyle\alpha\,r(c)$}\;-\;\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle\beta\,\kappa_{0}(c)$}\;-\;\gamma,\qquad\theta=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma),\qquad w(c)\;\triangleq\;1-\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathds{1}\bigl[\,0\in I(c)\,\bigr],`$ |  | (5) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\theta_{f}`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\theta}\;\sum_{c\,\in\,\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{C}_{f}}w(c)\,\log\Bigl(1+\exp\bigl[-\operatorname{sgn}\Delta(c)\;s_{\theta}(c)\bigr]\Bigr)\quad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,sixteen held-in cells per fold}}`$ |  |  |
|  | $`\displaystyle S`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\sum_{f=1}^{3}\;\sum_{c\,\in\,\mathcal{C}_{f}}w(c)\;\mathds{1}\bigl[\operatorname{sgn}s_{f}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\Delta(c)\bigr],\quad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,held-out score, at most 24}}`$ |  |  |

where $`s_{f}`$ is the score under $`\theta_{f}`$, the purple term pulls
a component toward the weights and the orange term toward the context, a
cell whose interval crosses zero counts one half in fit and score, and
the fit carries a ridge penalty on the standardised inputs
(Appendix [D](#A4 "Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
A held-out cell goes to $`{\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W}`$ if
$`s_{f}(c)>0`$, else to $`{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C}`$.

Figure 7: The rule. (a) Component summaries of both environments on the
plane, with the full-fit boundary (solid) and the three held-out
boundaries (dashed); (b) held-out score against the observed route gain,
24 cells with 95 percent intervals. Small black-edged markers: halves of
lessons and state facts split by item recurrence, used in no fit.

The three folds give $`\alpha`$ in $`[9.01,9.32]`$, $`\beta`$ in
$`[4.86,5.28]`$ and $`\gamma`$ in $`[0.70,0.94]`$, and the full fit
$`(11.29,5.73,1.28)`$ draws the boundary of
Figure [7](#S5.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Held-out fit. ‣ 5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")(a).
The held-out rule recovers the sign in 24 of 24 cells, 19 of them with
intervals clear of zero
(Figure [7](#S5.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Held-out fit. ‣ 5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")b),
and $`S=21.5/24{}`$. *The boundary runs between state facts and
lessons.* Locators and procedures are far from it (full-fit scores 2.52
and $`-`$4.45) and state facts and lessons close to it ($`-`$0.89 and
0.74), and the scores order the four components as their route gains do.
*The boundary also splits a component.* Split at the boundary by item
recurrence ($`r=0.377{}`$ for lessons, 0.394 for state facts), the half
above goes to the weights and the half below to the context: the route
gains are +2.5 and $`-`$1.8 for lessons and +2.9 and $`-`$2.1 for state
facts, and all twelve halves of the three families fall on the side the
rule gave them before the runs
(Figure [7](#S5.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Held-out fit. ‣ 5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
small markers;
Table [D.4](#A4.T4 "Table D.4 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
*The online quantity agrees with the proxy.* The state-conditionality
read from retrieval, $`\kappa(c)`$ of
Equation [4](#S3.E4 "In Recurrence and state-conditionality. ‣ 3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
agrees in rank with $`\kappa_{0}(c)`$ over the twelve MobileGym cells
(Spearman 0.56) and puts procedures and state facts above lessons and
locators on every backbone.

Table 1: Interventions. Gain over the base agent (points) on MobileGym
when one property of a component is changed: copying the training items
raises the training dose of every key, as recurrence across tasks does;
retrieving the notes by task text alone removes their state condition.
Subscripts are the std over three seeds. $`\Delta`$ is the shift from
the unmodified route above it ($`\uparrow`$rise / $`\downarrow`$drop),
averaged over the backbones the arm has.

#### One property at a time.

Changing one property moves a component the way the rule says.
Table [1](#S5.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 5.2 Interventions ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
reports the arms that change one property of a component, with the shift
from the unmodified route in its last column. *A larger training dose
moves procedures toward the weights.* A key that recurs in more tasks
contributes more samples to the weights route, so recurrence reaches the
weights as the number of updates a key receives. Copying every procedure
item eightfold before fine-tuning reproduces that dose and changes no
item: it moves the route gain of procedures from $`-`$4.2 to $`-`$0.8,
across zero on Qwen3-VL-8B (+1.0). Read as recurrence, eight copies
place procedures at $`r\approx 0.42{}`$, short of the boundary at their
state-conditionality ($`r\approx 0.44{}`$), and the route gain stays
below zero on average. State facts move by +3.6 and reach the context
route on Qwen3-VL-8B, and with two and four copies the gain grows with
the dose
(Table [E.1](#A5.T1 "Table E.1 ‣ E.1 All Intervention Arms ‣ Appendix E Full Results ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
At ten times the learning rate the weights route changes by +1.0 and
+1.0 points, and the route gains of procedures and state facts stay at
$`-`$3.3 and $`-`$3.2. *Removing the state condition removes most of the
context gain.* Serving the same notes retrieved by task text alone,
without their state condition, costs 3.4 points for state facts and 3.9
for procedures, so what the context route buys for these two components
is the condition, not the payload. Reading the condition from the
visible screen elements instead of the environment state keeps most of
it: the notes lose 0.7 points for procedures and 0.7 for state facts,
and both stay in the context (route gains $`-`$3.5 and $`-`$3.5).
*Shuffled items do nothing.* Shuffling the keys of the notes or of the
training samples leaves the base agent within 1.1 points
(Table [E.1](#A5.T1 "Table E.1 ‣ E.1 All Intervention Arms ‣ Appendix E Full Results ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")),
and random notes from other applications change it by $`-`$1.6; neither
the prompt format nor the fine-tuning itself produces the gains.

### 5.3 Readout and Conflict

![Refer to caption](2610.01787v1/figN1_arial.png)

Figure 8: Two illustrative episodes. Top: the locator comes from the
weights, the state fact and the procedure from the context. Bottom: a
note and a learned routine disagree on the entry type, and the agent
takes the action of the note. Screens are illustrative.

#### Stale weights, fresh notes.

When the weights and the context disagree, the more an item recurs, the
less often the agent follows the note and the more often it takes
neither action. To see what happens when the two disagree, we train the
weights on version 1 of the OpenApps applications ([Ullrich et al.,
2026](#bib.bib43)), serve notes from version 2, and record, at the first
step of a task where the two versions call for different actions,
whether the agent follows the note, the weights or neither
(Figure [8](#S5.F8 "Figure 8 ‣ 5.3 Readout and Conflict ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
bottom, shows one such step). On the new version, stale weights alone
change the base agent by $`-`$8.4 points and fresh notes alone by +3.3;
serving both scores between 2.7 and 12.7 points below notes alone.
*Recurrence shifts the outcome.* At the divergence step the agent
follows the note in 52 percent of the low-recurrence cases and 43
percent of the high-recurrence ones, the weights in 34 percent and 21
percent, and neither in 14 percent and 36 percent. This is the readout
result from the other side: the items the weights hold best are the
items a contradicting note corrects least, and when the weights hold a
stale version of such an item, the agent more often takes neither
action.

ScaleCUA-7B; subscripts are the std over three seeds. Self-retry uses

MobileGym backbones, appears in the $`\Delta`$ column (points; shade
$`\propto`$ gain).

#### Against the alternatives.

Routing by the held-out rule beats every whole-trajectory baseline and,
on average over backbones, the better single destination.
Table [2](#S5.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 5.4 Routing against the Alternatives ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
compares them on the same held-out instances, with the gain of routing
over each row on MobileGym in its last column (compute and tokens in
Appendix [H](#A8 "Appendix H Compute and Tokens ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
Routed sends each component where the held-out rule says, so its
assignment on a backbone is fixed before that backbone is trained.
Fitted on one half of the held-out templates instead, the rule gives the
same assignment in five of the six folds, and routing leads the better
single destination on the other half by +3.7 to +5.1 points on MobileGym
and +2.4 to +2.6 on AndroidWorld
(Table [D.3](#A4.T3 "Table D.3 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
On the full set it exceeds the better single destination on every
MobileGym backbone, by +4.4 points on average; on AndroidWorld it
exceeds it by +5.0 with Qwen3-VL-8B and by +3.2 with ScaleCUA-7B, and
matches it with GUI-Owl-8B. *The single destinations fail on different
components.* All to the context forgoes the weights gain of locators,
all to the weights the context gain of procedures and state facts;
routing keeps both
(Figure [8](#S5.F8 "Figure 8 ‣ 5.3 Readout and Conflict ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
top). *Components carry what whole trajectories do not.* The best
whole-trajectory baseline, three sampled attempts with self-retry, is
+9.3 points below routing, and fine-tuning on whole trajectories,
retrieval of one trajectory or of ten step records, and
context-then-distill all stay below the single destinations. The lead
comes from what the components extract: localization samples for
locators, preference pairs drawn from failed attempts for lessons, and
notes matched to the current state for procedures and state facts.
Without the state match, the notes of procedures and state facts gain
+1.3 and +1.6, as ten step records retrieved by task text do (+1.4);
retrieved by the state signature instead, the same records gain +1.6
(Table [E.1](#A5.T1 "Table E.1 ‣ E.1 All Intervention Arms ‣ Appendix E Full Results ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")),
still 3.6 and 3.4 points below the notes of procedures and state facts.
Fine-tuning on whole trajectories gains +0.7, about as much as
procedures in the weights (+1.0). *The assignment is what matters.* The
reverse assignment loses +8.9 points against routing on MobileGym and
+6.7 on AndroidWorld, and the in-sample rule assigns the same routes, so
routing by the full fit differs by $`-`$0.2.

## 6 Producer and Consumer Shifts

Observation 2 found that notes travel from a producer to a consumer and
fine-tuning samples do not. This section measures three gaps between the
two models before any transfer, shows which gap each route pays for, and
reads off what survives a change of producer or of consumer.

Figure 9: The three gaps. (a–c) Family-level gain of the procedures
route against the information gap, the producer’s ability and the policy
gap: 720 cells, binned means with 95 percent intervals from a bootstrap
over the 15 producer–consumer pairs. (d) Five consumers on their own
procedures: context, weights, and weights from own successes only.

### 6.1 Three Gaps

#### Gaps and gains.

The context route pays for information and the weights route for policy
agreement. For a producer $`p`$, a consumer $`q`$ and a task family
$`\varphi`$, let $`\sigma_{\varphi}(m)`$ be the pass rate of model $`m`$
on the family in its own pool, $`X(p,q)`$ the states the two pools share
under exact matching, $`a_{m}(x)`$ the action of $`m`$ at state $`x`$,
$`U_{\varphi}`$ the held-out success on the family and $`U_{0}(m)`$ that
of model $`m`$ alone. The three gaps, the two gains and the practice
term are

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle g_{I}(p,q,\varphi)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;\sigma_{\varphi}(p)\,\bigl[1-\sigma_{\varphi}(q)\bigr],\qquad g_{P}(p,q)\;\triangleq\;\frac{1}{|X(p,q)|}\sum_{x\in X(p,q)}\mathds{1}\bigl[\,a_{q}(x)\neq a_{p}(x)\,\bigr],`$ |  | (6) |
|  | $`\displaystyle g_{A}(p)`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;U_{0}(p),\qquad\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentC!40}$\displaystyle G_{C}(p,q,\varphi)$}\;\triangleq\;U_{\varphi}({\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C_{P}^{\,p}})-U_{\varphi}(q),\qquad\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentW!45}$\displaystyle G_{W}(p,q,\varphi)$}\;\triangleq\;U_{\varphi}({\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W_{P}^{\,p}})-U_{\varphi}(q),`$ |  |  |
|  | $`\displaystyle\hbox{\pagecolor{AccentW!45}$\displaystyle P(q)$}`$ | $`\displaystyle\triangleq\;U({\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W_{P}^{\dagger}})-U_{0}(q),\qquad{\color[rgb]{0.35,0.35,0.35}\text{\scriptsize$\triangleright$\,$q$ trained on its own successes only, from families it already solves}}`$ |  |  |

so that $`g_{I}`$ is the share of the family that the producer solves
and the consumer does not, $`g_{P}`$ the rate at which the consumer
would act differently from the producer on the same state, and $`g_{A}`$
the producer’s own success.
Figure [9](#S6.F9 "Figure 9 ‣ 6 Producer and Consumer Shifts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
places the 720 cells of 15 producer–consumer pairs on 16 task families
against the three gaps; the information and policy gaps vary almost
independently across the cells (Spearman $`-`$0.13). *Information
carries the context gain.* The context gain rises with the information
gap from +0.2 points in the lowest sixth of the cells to +11.3 in the
highest (Spearman 0.65); the producer’s ability tracks it at 0.20 on its
own and at 0.05 once the information gap is held fixed, and with the
consumer’s headroom on the family held fixed the information gap keeps
0.65. A note pays when it says something the consumer does not know,
whoever wrote it. *Policy disagreement takes the weights gain away.* The
weights gain falls with the policy gap from +4.0 points in the lowest
sixth to $`-`$5.7 in the highest ($`-`$0.52; $`-`$0.52 given the
information gap) and rises with the information gap (0.49): fine-tuning
buys the same information as the notes and pays for it on every state
where the producer’s action is one the consumer would not take.

### 6.2 Producer Shifts

#### Along the ladder.

A larger producer widens the information gap, a foreign one opens a
policy gap, and each route follows its own. For the Qwen3-VL-8B
consumer, the 4B, 8B and 32B producers of its family have information
gaps of 0.04, 0.06 and 0.08 and the same policy gap (0.16); their notes
gain more in that order, and in the weights only the consumer’s own
samples gain
(Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Producer and Consumer ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")a),
the practice term of
Equation [6](#S6.E6 "In Gaps and gains. ‣ 6.1 Three Gaps ‣ 6 Producer and Consumer Shifts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").
*A foreign producer is a policy gap, not an information gap.* The
GUI-Owl-8B pool has the information gap of a same-family producer (0.07)
and a policy gap of 0.46: its notes help as much as the consumer’s own,
and its samples hurt
(Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Producer and Consumer ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")b).
Retraining that producer on the consumer’s successes closes the policy
gap (0.17), leaves the information gap (0.07), and brings its samples to
what a same-family producer’s give.

### 6.3 Consumer Shifts

#### Consumer upgrade.

After an upgrade the notes keep their value and the weights start over,
because what the weights bought was practice. When the consumer moves
from the 8B to the 32B model of the same family, the notes of the 8B
producer still give the 32B consumer +3.2 points and the same samples in
its weights $`-`$1.4. *Practice needs no producer.* On all five
consumers, fine-tuning on the consumer’s own successes alone, from
families it already solves, matches its full procedures within 1.1
points
(Figure [9](#S6.F9 "Figure 9 ‣ 6 Producer and Consumer Shifts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")d).
A note library therefore carries over a change of consumer, and the
weights route is rebuilt from the new consumer’s own trajectories.

## 7 Conclusion

We presented component routing, which sends each component of a GUI
agent’s own experience to the context or to the weights by two
properties measured on the pool before any training, recurrence and
state-conditionality. On the same items and held-out tasks across three
backbone families and two environments, one pool has two destinations:
locators and lessons win in the weights, procedures and state facts in
the context. A rule in the two properties recovers the destination of
every component on a held-out family and of both halves of a component
split at its boundary, and routing by it beats every whole-trajectory
baseline and, on average, the better single destination of each
backbone. Note readout falls once the same component is in the weights,
most for the components that recur most; context gains grow with the
information gap and weights gains shrink with the policy gap, so where
experience belongs also depends on who produced it and who consumes it.

### A.2 Extraction

Two rule-based extractors read the accessibility state and the action of
every step in a pool and emit the items of the four components: a strict
one keeps element names verbatim, and a lenient one normalizes them
before keys are compared. Every pool is built with the lenient
extractor. Items are rendered as notes and as training samples in the
fixed templates of
Appendix [I.3](#A9.SS3 "I.3 Notes Block ‣ Appendix I Prompts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

## Appendix B Arms and Protocol

This appendix gives the design constants behind
Section [3](#S3 "3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"):
the two environments and their splits, the pools, every arm, and the
interaction budget. All of them were fixed before the runs; measured
outcomes are in the main text and in
Appendix [E](#A5 "Appendix E Full Results ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

### B.1 Environments and Splits

#### MobileGym.

MobileGym has 20 applications and 416 task templates in 24 suites, split
by the benchmark into 160 training and 256 test templates. A template
instantiates a task with sampled parameters, and the environment judges
an episode by comparing the final application state with the target
state. Applications are ranked by their number of training templates,
and every fourth application in that ranking is held out as unseen; this
gives 5 unseen applications. Training templates whose applications are
all seen form the experience pool (122 templates). Test templates whose
applications are all seen form the seen split (165), test templates
whose applications are all unseen form the unseen split (59), and the 32
test templates that touch both are reported separately and enter no
main-text number. Each held-out template is instantiated up to 8 times
per seed (126 templates have 8 instances and 98 have one), with
parameters fixed by (template, instance, seed) and stored, so every arm
runs the same 1 106 instances per seed.

#### AndroidWorld.

AndroidWorld has 116 tasks over 20 applications, judged by the official
evaluator. The unseen tier takes 8 of the 20 applications (identifiers
audiorec, draw, joplin, notes, osmand, retro, simplecal and vlc). The 58
held-out tasks are instantiated four times per seed, 232 instances, and
the remaining tasks form the pool. The state signature is the set of
visible accessibility nodes (class, resource id, normalized text),
capped at 500 nodes, together with the package and activity. Locator
keys are (application, class, resource id or text); procedure keys are
three consecutive action-target signatures; state-fact keys are the node
signatures present in the successful state and absent in the failed one,
at most five; lesson keys are as on MobileGym. Actions follow the
official action space through each backbone’s own adapter.

#### Pools.

On MobileGym the base agent of each family runs every experience
template 20 times at temperature 1 with a fresh instance each time, once
per seed. Every step records the screenshot, the environment state, the
element list, the action and its target. On AndroidWorld the pool runs
each pool task ten times. The four component extractors run on the pool
once, and the recurrence and state-conditionality of every item are
computed from the pool alone. The coordinates of a cell are the mean
recurrence and the median state-conditionality over the items of its
component, merged over the three seeds. For the producer ladder of
Section [6](#S6 "6 Producer and Consumer Shifts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
the pools are repeated with the 4B and 32B members of the Qwen3-VL
family and the 32B member of the GUI-Owl family as producers.

#### Producer–consumer batch.

The measurements of
Sections [4.2](#S4.SS2 "4.2 Producer and Consumer ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
and [6](#S6 "6 Producer and Consumer Shifts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
come from one batch of their own. Every procedures adapter of this batch
trains on 5 600 samples drawn from the producer’s pool (1 900 for the
32B consumers), so every producer enters the weights at the same
training budget, and its own-procedure arms are separate runs from those
of
Table [1](#S5.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 5.2 Interventions ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").
The batch groups the held-out templates into 16 task families: eight
single-application suites, three cross-application suites and five kinds
of task shared across applications (search and filter, compose and send,
settings toggles, media control and multi-step forms).

#### Version change.

The conflict measurement of
Section [5.3](#S5.SS3 "5.3 Readout and Conflict ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
uses OpenApps ([Ullrich et al., 2026](#bib.bib43)), whose 15 tasks over
six applications exist in two application versions. Each version is
sampled 20 times per task. The weights route is trained on version 1
items, the notes are served from version 2, and every arm runs on all
three families and three seeds, on 150 version-2 instances per seed (ten
goal variants per task). At the first state where the two versions’
successful procedures diverge, the arm’s action is compared with the
version-2 note and with the version-1 weights without notes, under the
same-action rule of
Appendix [B.3](#A2.SS3 "B.3 Interaction Budget ‣ Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents");
the shares of
Section [5.3](#S5.SS3 "5.3 Readout and Conflict ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
count 520 such steps, 312 on GUI-Owl-8B and 104 on each other family.

#### Evaluation.

All arms use greedy decoding, the official step limit, the native screen
resolution, and the same stored instances. An episode is a success when
the environment judge accepts the final state. Every reported difference
between two arms is paired over (template, instance, seed) and carries a
percentile interval from 10 000 bootstrap resamples of the paired
differences. Cells pool the three seeds; per-seed values give the
subscripts of the tables.

### B.2 Arms

The arm names below are the ones of the delivered result tables. Unless
stated, an arm runs on all three families, both environments and all
seeds.

Base agent and single-component routes:

- •
  none: the base agent with the evaluation prompt and no experience; the
  zero of every gain.
- •
  C_G, C_P, C_F, C_L: the context route of one component. At every step
  the items of the same application are ranked by the Jaccard similarity
  of their source state signature to the current one. Exact matches (at
  least 0.9) come first and relaxed matches (at least 0.5) fill up to
  five notes, appended to the prompt as a notes block. Procedures
  retrieve the skill file of the most similar task text first and the
  step-level items within it second.
- •
  C_c_exact, C_c_relaxed: the context route restricted to the exact or
  to the relaxed tier; their difference against none gives the online
  state-conditionality of
  Equation [4](#S3.E4 "In Recurrence and state-conditionality. ‣ 3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").
- •
  W_G, W_P, W_F: the weights route of one component, a LoRA adapter
  fine-tuned on the component’s items rendered as samples
  (Appendix [C](#A3 "Appendix C Training Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
  W_L trains the adapter by preference optimization, with the successful
  action as chosen and the failed action as rejected.
- •
  CW_G, CW_P, CW_F, CW_L: the weights-route adapter served with the
  notes of the same component. Every note-bearing step also runs once
  without the note, which gives the after-training readout of
  Section [4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Readout after Training ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

Aggregate arms:

- •
  all_C: the four libraries served together, at most two notes per
  component and eight in total, exact matches first.
- •
  all_W: one adapter trained on the locator, procedure and state-fact
  samples together, then preference-optimized on the lessons from that
  adapter.
- •
  routed: each component sent where the rule fitted with the family held
  out says
  (Appendix [D](#A4 "Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
  The components sent to the weights are trained as in all_W restricted
  to those components; the components sent to the context are served
  with the all_C quota. The assignment is written to disk before the
  adapter is trained.
- •
  anti_routed: the same with every destination reversed.
- •
  routed_self: the destinations read from the family’s own observed
  signs, used as an in-sample routing reference; GUI-Owl-8B only.

Whole-trajectory baselines:

- •
  B1_bon: three samples of the same instance at temperature 1. The
  main-text number keeps the first attempt that the agent declares
  complete, and the last attempt otherwise (self-retry).
- •
  B2_wholetraj_sft: supervised fine-tuning on every step of every
  successful pool episode.
- •
  B3_wholetraj_k1: the action sequence of the single successful pool
  episode with the most similar task text, pasted into the prompt.
- •
  B4_atomic_k10: ten step-level records (state change, action) retrieved
  by task-text similarity, without state matching.
- •
  B5_icl_distill_P, B5_icl_distill_F: context-then-distill. The context
  route of the component runs on the experience templates as a teacher
  (ten episodes per template), and its successful trajectories are
  fine-tuned into the weights without a notes block.

Interventions:

- •
  W_P_dup$`m`$, W_F_dup$`m`$: the source episodes of the component are
  copied $`m`$ times into the pool before extraction, so the training
  set of the weights route, and with it the training dose of every key,
  grows $`m`$-fold while the notes do not change; $`m=8`$ on all three
  families, $`m\in\{2,4\}`$ on GUI-Owl-8B only.
- •
  C_P_destate, C_F_destate: the same notes retrieved by task-text
  similarity only, without the state signature.
- •
  C_P_elem, C_F_elem: the same notes retrieved with a signature read
  from the screen, the set of visible elements as (role, normalized
  name) pairs, in place of the environment state; thresholds and ranking
  unchanged.
- •
  W_P_lr$`\eta`$, W_F_lr$`\eta`$: the samples of W_P and W_F, trained at
  learning rate $`\eta\in\{3{\times}10^{-5},10^{-4}\}`$ instead of
  $`10^{-5}`$.
- •
  W_c_rhi, W_c_rlo, C_c_rhi, C_c_rlo, $`c\in\{L,F\}`$: the items of
  lessons or of state facts of each pool split by item recurrence at the
  full-fit boundary for the mean $`\kappa_{0}`$ of the component
  ($`r=0.377{}`$ for lessons, 0.394 for state facts), each half sent to
  the weights and to the context as the whole component is.
- •
  B4_atomic_state_k10: the step-level records of B4_atomic_k10 retrieved
  by the state signature, exact matches first, instead of by task text.

The last four groups run on MobileGym with all three families and three
seeds.

Controls and reference arms:

- •
  random_cards: five items drawn at random from other applications, in
  the same format.
- •
  shuffle_c_C: the payloads of a component’s items permuted across its
  keys; shuffle_c_W: the labels of the training samples permuted across
  samples (coordinates for locators, actions for procedures and state
  facts, chosen and rejected swapped for lessons); GUI-Owl-8B only.
- •
  Sensitivity variants of the context and weights routes
  (Appendix [F](#A6 "Appendix F Sensitivity ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")):
  Jaccard thresholds of 0.8 and 0.6, three or ten notes, adapter ranks
  64 and 128, pools of five or ten episodes per template, library caps
  of 100 and 300 items, a flat notes block of five items without
  components, and routing by the online state-conditionality;
  GUI-Owl-8B, seed 0.

### B.3 Interaction Budget

All arms use the same held-out instances and the official per-episode
step limit. Each arm runs one episode per instance, except self-retry,
which runs three attempts. The two routes consume the same items: the
notes and the training samples of a component are rendered from the same
extracted items of the same pool. Two quantities the budget does not
equalize are reported in
Appendix [H](#A8 "Appendix H Compute and Tokens ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"):
the notes block that the context route adds to every prompt, and the
adapter training run that the weights route adds. Two actions count as
the same when they are of the same type and, for taps, hit the same
element or land within 2 percent of the screen diagonal of each other;
for text entry, carry the same stripped text; for scrolls, go in the
same direction. This rule decides the readout of
Section [4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Readout after Training ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
the policy gap of
Section [6](#S6 "6 Producer and Consumer Shifts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
and the conflict outcome of
Section [5.3](#S5.SS3 "5.3 Readout and Conflict ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

## Appendix C Training Setup

Every weights-route arm is a LoRA adapter trained on the base agent of
its family and merged before serving. The vision tower stays frozen, and
a weights-route arm is evaluated with the prompt of the base agent,
without a notes block. Every adapter of every family uses the same
configuration, fixed before the runs: rank 16, $`\alpha`$ 32, three
epochs, learning rate $`10^{-5}`$.
Table [C.1](#A3.T1 "Table C.1 ‣ Aggregate adapters. ‣ C.1 Weights Route ‣ Appendix C Training Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
lists the samples of every adapter and its token accuracy on a held-in
tenth of them.

### C.1 Weights Route

#### Samples.

A locator item becomes one sample per source step: the screenshot and
the instruction to tap the named element, with the tap coordinates as
the target. A procedure item becomes the step-by-step samples of the
successful trajectories of its task family, with the sub-goal sequence
as the thought. A state-fact item becomes its source step, task,
screenshot and history, with the predicate as the thought and the action
as the target. A lesson item becomes a preference pair on its source
state, the successful action as chosen and the failed action as
rejected, trained by preference optimization from the same adapter
configuration. Success-filtered fine-tuning takes every step of every
successful pool episode; context-then-distill takes the successful
teacher episodes of the context route, at the sample count of the
weights route of the same component; the copy interventions repeat the
source episodes of a component before extraction, so their sample counts
are the multiples listed in the table.

#### Aggregate adapters.

All to the weights trains one adapter on the locator, procedure and
state-fact samples together and then runs the lesson preference stage
from that adapter. The routed and reverse-assignment adapters follow the
same two stages restricted to the components each assignment sends to
the weights; their assignment is written to disk before the adapter is
trained.
````
