````math
### C.2 Context Route

The notes of a component are its items rendered as one line each in a
fixed template. A locator note names the element, its role and its
position; a procedure note gives the sub-goal sequence of its skill file
and the next sub-goal; a state-fact note states the condition that must
hold before its action; a lesson note names the action to avoid in its
state and the action to take instead. At every step the library of the
current application is ranked by the Jaccard similarity between each
item’s source state signature and the current signature, exact matches
(at least 0.9) before relaxed matches (at least 0.5). The top five notes
are appended to the prompt as a notes block, and the rest of the prompt
is the base agent’s. Procedures are retrieved in two stages: the skill
file of the most similar task text, then the step-level items within it.
The aggregate context arms serve at most two notes per component and
eight in total, exact matches first. Prompt tokens are recorded with and
without the notes block on every step and enter
Appendix [H](#A8 "Appendix H Compute and Tokens ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

## Appendix D The Rule Fit

The rule of
Section [5.1](#S5.SS1 "5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
is fitted by a procedure fixed before the runs. This appendix gives its
notation, the objective as implemented, the routine as run, and the
per-cell held-out table behind
Figure [7](#S5.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Held-out fit. ‣ 5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

### D.1 Notation and Objective

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Symbol |  Description |
| $`\mathcal{C}`$ |  the twenty-four cells, one per (component, backbone family, environment) |
| $`\mathcal{C}_{f}`$ |  the eight cells of family $`f`$; the fold that holds $`f`$ out fits on $`\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{C}_{f}`$ |
| $`r(c),\ \kappa_{0}(c)`$ |  the pool coordinates of cell $`c`$: mean recurrence and median state-conditionality of its items |
| $`\Delta(c),\ I(c)`$ |  the route gain of $`c`$ and its 95 percent paired-bootstrap interval |
| $`y(c)`$ |  the sign of $`\Delta(c)`$, $`+1`$ toward the weights and $`-1`$ toward the context |
| $`w(c)`$ |  the weight of the cell, $`\tfrac{1}{2}`$ when $`0\in I(c)`$ and $`1`$ otherwise |
| $`z(c)`$ |  the standardised coordinates, each of $`r`$ and $`\kappa_{0}`$ centred and scaled by the mean and standard deviation over the cells in the fit |
| $`u,\ b`$ |  the two slopes on $`z(c)`$ and the unpenalised intercept |
| $`\lambda`$ |  the ridge strength, one over the number of cells in the fit |
| $`s_{\theta}(c)`$ |  the score on the raw scale, $`\alpha\,r(c)-\beta\,\kappa_{0}(c)-\gamma`$, obtained from $`(u,b)`$ by undoing the standardisation |
| $`S`$ |  the held-out score, $`\sum_{c}w(c)\,\mathds{1}[\operatorname{sgn}s_{f}(c)=y(c)]`$, at most 24 |

The fit minimises

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\frac{1}{\sum_{c}w(c)}\sum_{c\,\in\,\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{C}_{f}}w(c)\,\log\Bigl(1+\exp\bigl[-y(c)\,(u^{\top}z(c)+b)\bigr]\Bigr)\;+\;\frac{\lambda}{2}\,\lVert u\rVert^{2}
``` |  | (D.1) |

by full-batch gradient descent from zero with step size $`0.1`$ for
twenty thousand iterations, as fixed before the runs. The intercept is
not penalised, and the result does not change under ten times as many
iterations. A cell of the held-out family goes to the weights when
$`s_{f}(c)>0`$ and to the context otherwise. The point count of
Section [5.1](#S5.SS1 "5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
is the number of held-out cells whose predicted sign equals $`y(c)`$;
$`S`$ weights the cells whose interval crosses zero by one half.

### D.2 The Routine

Algorithm [1](#alg1 "Algorithm 1 ‣ D.2 The Routine ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
is the complete procedure behind
Sections [3](#S3 "3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
and [5](#S5 "5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"):
it measures the pool, fits the rule with one backbone family held out,
routes every component of the held-out family by the fitted sign, trains
or serves accordingly, and reads the result on the held-out instances.
Notation follows
Section [3](#S3 "3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
and
Appendix [D.1](#A4.SS1 "D.1 Notation and Objective ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").

Input: the base agent $`\pi_{0}`$ of family $`f`$, its pool
$`\mathcal{D}`$ of trajectories on the training templates, the held-out
instances $`\mathcal{H}`$, the cells $`\mathcal{C}`$ of the other
families with their signs, the extractor $`\phi`$, ridge strength
$`\lambda`$

1:  Phase I: Measure $`\triangleright`$ before any training; pool only
2:  extract from every trajectory in $`\mathcal{D}`$ the items of the
four components with $`\phi`$: a key, a payload and a state condition
each 3:  for each component $`c`$, set $`r(c)`$ to the mean over its
items of the share of unrelated tasks whose episodes contain the key,
and $`\kappa_{0}(c)`$ to the median state-conditionality over its valued
items

4:  Phase II: Fit $`\triangleright`$ family $`f`$ is not in the fit 5:
 standardise $`r`$ and $`\kappa_{0}`$ on the sixteen held-in cells
$`\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{C}_{f}`$ 6:  $`(u,b)\leftarrow`$ the
minimiser of
Equation [D.1](#A4.E1 "In D.1 Notation and Objective ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
by gradient descent from zero 7:  for each component $`c`$ of family
$`f`$:
$`s_{f}(c)\leftarrow\alpha_{f}\,r(c)-\beta_{f}\,\kappa_{0}(c)-\gamma_{f}`$

8:  Phase III: Route $`\triangleright`$ one destination per component,
fixed before training

9:  for all components $`c`$ with $`s_{f}(c)>0`$ do 10:   render every
item of $`c`$ as a training sample; fine-tune an adapter on $`\pi_{0}`$
in the frozen configuration of
Appendix [C](#A3 "Appendix C Training Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
(lessons by preference pairs, the other components by supervised steps)

11:  end for

12:  for all components $`c`$ with $`s_{f}(c)\leq 0`$ do 13:   render
every item of $`c`$ as a note with its state condition; at each step
retrieve at most two notes of $`c`$, the quota of all to the context,
whose key matches the current screen and whose condition holds, and
place them in the prompt

14:  end for

15:  Phase IV: Evaluate $`\triangleright`$ same held-out instances and
per-episode step limit 16:  run the routed agent on $`\mathcal{H}`$ with
the adapter of Phase III and the notes of Phase III 17:  pair each
episode with the base agent and the single-destination arms on the same
instance and seed; report the mean difference with a paired bootstrap of
10 000 resamples

18:  return the assignment
$`\{c\mapsto{\color[rgb]{0.575,0.4844,0.6531}W}\text{ or }{\color[rgb]{0.5371,0.4039,0.26}C}\}`$
and the held-out success

Algorithm 1 Component routing, one held-out family (Measure, Fit, Route
to the weights, Route to the context, and Evaluate)

### D.3 Held-out Table

Table [D.1](#A4.T1 "Table D.1 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
gives the coefficients of the full fit and of the three folds;
Table [D.2](#A4.T2 "Table D.2 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
gives the twenty-four cells with their pool coordinates, route gains,
weights and held-out scores. The three folds agree in sign with the
observed route gain in 24 of 24 cells, 19 of them with intervals clear
of zero, for $`S=21.5/24{}`$. The full fit draws the boundary of
Figure [7](#S5.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Held-out fit. ‣ 5.1 A Rule in Two Properties ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")(a)
and agrees with all twenty-four cells in sample. Under every fold the
held-out family receives the same assignment, locators and lessons to
the weights and procedures and state facts to the context, and this is
the assignment the routed arm was trained with.
Figure [D.1](#A4.F1 "Figure D.1 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
draws the four boundaries and the held-out scores against the observed
gains.
Table [D.3](#A4.T3 "Table D.3 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
repeats the fit on one half of the held-out templates and reads routing
on the other half.

#### Halves of a component.

Lessons and state facts lie closest to the boundary, so each of them is
split by item recurrence at the full-fit boundary for its mean
$`\kappa_{0}`$, and both halves are sent to both routes
(Appendix [B](#A2 "Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
The halves differ in recurrence and hardly in state-conditionality, and
no fit used them: their destinations were read off the full fit before
the runs, and the fold that holds a family out gives the same side.
Table [D.4](#A4.T4 "Table D.4 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
lists the twelve halves; every half above the boundary is better off in
the weights and every half below it in the context, with intervals clear
of zero, by +4.3 points between the two halves of lessons and +4.9
between those of state facts.

## Appendix E Full Results

The tables of this appendix expand the main-text measurements into their
per-family form. Cells are means over the three seeds with the seed
standard deviation as subscript where an arm has three seeds; every
difference is paired over (template, instance, seed). The twenty-four
cells of the rule are in
Table [D.2](#A4.T2 "Table D.2 ‣ Halves of a component. ‣ D.3 Held-out Table ‣ Appendix D The Rule Fit ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents");
Figure [E.1](#A5.F1 "Figure E.1 ‣ Appendix E Full Results ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
draws them with their intervals and adds the gains on seen and unseen
applications.

## Appendix F Sensitivity

Each variant of
Table [F.1](#A6.T1 "Table F.1 ‣ Notes block and rule input. ‣ Appendix F Sensitivity ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
changes one setting of a default arm on GUI-Owl-8B, seed 0, and leaves
everything else as in
Appendix [B](#A2 "Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").
The table reports the gain of the default arm over the base agent on the
same instances, the gain of the variant, and their difference.

#### Matching thresholds.

The exact and relaxed tiers of the context route move from 0.9 and 0.5
to 0.8 and 0.6, for all four components.

#### Notes per step.

The context route of locators and state facts serves three or ten notes
instead of five.

#### Adapter rank.

The weights route of locators and state facts is trained at rank 64 and
128 instead of 16, at the same number of epochs.

#### Pool size.

Both routes of locators and state facts are built from nested subsets of
five and ten episodes per template instead of 20.

#### Library cap.

The locator library is capped at 100 and 300 items.

#### Notes block and rule input.

All to the context serves five notes without the per-component quota.
Routing reads the online state-conditionality of
Equation [4](#S3.E4 "In Recurrence and state-conditionality. ‣ 3 Experimental Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
instead of $`\kappa_{0}`$ when the rule assigns the destinations.

## Appendix H Compute and Tokens

Every arm is evaluated on the same held-out instances
(Appendix [B.3](#A2.SS3 "B.3 Interaction Budget ‣ Appendix B Arms and Protocol ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")).
Two accounts differ between arms: the training compute of the adapter an
arm trains, and the prompt tokens it spends per episode.
Table [H.1](#A8.T1 "Table H.1 ‣ Appendix H Compute and Tokens ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
lists both for every arm of
Table [2](#S5.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 5.4 Routing against the Alternatives ‣ 5 The Routing Rule ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents")
on MobileGym with GUI-Owl-8B, as means over seeds; the other two
families train the same arms at the same configuration on pools of the
same size. Adapter training is booked per training sample at the rates
of one H100, and pool sampling at a fixed per-episode rate that every
arm reading the pool shares. Prompt tokens are counted on every step
with the notes block present, so the ratio to the base agent is the
token cost of the context route at the interaction budget of the paper.

## Appendix I Prompts

Three kinds of text reach the model: the system prompt of each backbone,
the user turn of each step, and the notes block that the context route
appends to the user turn. The MobileGym applications are Chinese, and so
are the Qwen3-VL prompt, the notes block and every note; they are
reproduced verbatim below, each followed by an English rendering. Line
breaks marked by a grey arrow are for display only.

### I.1 Agent Prompts

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

*English rendering of the Qwen3-VL prompt.* You are an expert operator
of a mobile GUI agent. Given the task, the current screenshot and the
history of operations, analyse the screen and output one action to
interact with the phone and complete the task. Coordinates have their
origin at the top left, $`x`$ to the right and $`y`$ downward, both in
the range 0 to 1000. The fifteen actions, in JSON, are click, double
tap, long press, type (with an optional point and an optional clear
flag), swipe, drag, back, home, recent apps, enter, wait, open app,
submit an answer, complete the task with a short note, and abort with a
reason. The output is a \<THINK\> block that states what the screen
shows, what to do next and which element to operate, followed by an
\<ANSWER\> block with one JSON action. Coordinates must be numbers in 0
to 1000, the JSON must be valid, decisions follow the screenshot,
questions are answered with the answer action, and the complete action
is used only after the task has been carried out.

### I.2 User Turn

The user turn of a step carries the current screenshot and, on the first
step of the history window, the instruction text below with the task and
the summary of previous actions filled in. GUI-Owl-1.5-8B keeps a window
of the last four steps, each as its screenshot followed by the full
model output of that step, and lists older steps as one line each;
ScaleCUA-7B sends the current screenshot with a one-line history;
Qwen3-VL-8B keeps its previous outputs as text and sends the screenshot
of the current step only. A weights-route arm and the base agent receive
exactly these messages. A context-route arm receives the same messages
plus one text part appended after the current screenshot, the notes
block of
Appendix [I.3](#A9.SS3 "I.3 Notes Block ‣ Appendix I Prompts ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
and nothing is appended on a step without retrieved items. For the
readout probe of
Section [4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Readout after Training ‣ 4 Observations ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents"),
every step that received a notes block is also run once without it; both
outputs are logged, and the action with the block is the one executed.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

*English rendering of the Qwen3-VL user turn.* The first turn is the
line “\[Task\]” followed by the task; later turns are “\[Step $`i`$\]”
followed by the current screenshot.

### I.3 Notes Block

The block is one text part with a fixed header and one line per
retrieved item, in retrieval order; the aggregate arms list the
components in the order locators, procedures, state facts, lessons. Two
headers exist, one per coordinate frame.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

*English rendering of the header.* “\[Experience notes\] (from past use
of the same application, for reference only; coordinates are on the same
0 to 1000 scale as the screenshot; the current screenshot and task take
precedence)”. The ScaleCUA header states instead that coordinates are in
the pixel frame the model sees, 952 by 2156.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

*English rendering of the templates.* A locator note reads “On this page
of {app}, the element ‘{name}’ ({role}) is tapped at ({x}, {y})”. A
procedure note reads “In {app}, after ‘{name1}’ and ‘{name2}’, the next
step is usually ‘{name3}”’. A state-fact note reads “Before doing
‘{name}’ in {app}, the following must hold: {pred1}; {pred2}; …”, with
at most five predicates. A lesson note reads “In this state of {app}, do
not do ‘{name_fail}’; do ‘{name_success}’ instead”. A predicate is one
of three forms over a path of the application state, with list
identifiers replaced by a placeholder: “{path} exists”, “{path} is set
(non-empty)”, or “{path} must be the value the task requires”; keys that
change on every run, such as timestamps and identifiers, never enter a
predicate. Retrieval and the per-step quota are those of
Appendix [C.2](#A3.SS2 "C.2 Context Route ‣ Appendix C Training Setup ‣ Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents").
````
